title: reservations.reservations.update
description: Edits an existing reservation. The change passes the SAME availability gate the booking passed (party-size limits, advance window, blocked days, a slot with room), evaluated on the EFFECTIVE values (reservations#14). Since reservations#50 it also carries WHO is asking (`channel`, and `customer_id` on the customer channel): editing a reservation on behalf of a guest is refused when that reservation belongs to somebody else, and the customer channel cannot write `table_id` or `internal_notes`.

channel.description: Who is editing the reservation: `staff` (someone operating the hub, the default — the reservations screen sends no channel and keeps editing every table: the dining room is its own) or `customer` (the guest through an external channel, bound to say who they are with `customer_id`, and unable to write `table_id` or `internal_notes` — those are the restaurant's).

customer_id.description: Who is asking, on the `customer` channel (reservations#50): the id of that guest in `customers`, as the external channel resolved them (the WhatsApp automation looks the guest up by phone before listing anything). The edit is refused when the reservation belongs to somebody else. MANDATORY whenever `channel` is `customer`, and applied by the handler rather than here: it is a rule about two fields at once, decided against the reservation row this schema cannot see. The staff channel never sends it.
